# Gladiator II: The Art and Making of the Ridley Scott Film

Gladiator II: The Art and Making of the Ridley Scott Film is an official behind-the-scenes companion book written by British filmmaker, double BAFTA- and Grierson-nominated documentarian, and author John Walsh. Published by Abrams Books on March 18, 2025, it chronicles the production of the 2024 epic historical action film Gladiator II, directed by Ridley Scott and released by Paramount Pictures. The 224-page hardcover (with an ebook edition available) includes a foreword by Scott and features approximately 500 full-color illustrations, providing an in-depth visual and narrative examination of the film's creation.
Background and publication
Walsh, founder of Walsh Bros Ltd (a leading UK production company) and a trustee of the Ray and Diana Harryhausen Foundation, was commissioned by Abrams Books and Paramount Pictures to document the sequel. He is known for his series of official film companion books, including volumes on Conan the Barbarian, The Wicker Man, The Third Man, Harryhausen: The Lost Movies, Flash Gordon, and others.
The book was released in hardcover format on March 18, 2025 (ISBN 978-1-4197-8016-5), priced at $50, with an ebook edition (ISBN 979-8-8870-7593-8) priced around $31.10. Its large trim size (11 5/16 × 10 3/8 inches) suits its coffee-table style emphasis on visuals.Promotion included a book signing event at Forbidden Planet's London Megastore on April 12, 2025, where Walsh signed copies and engaged with fans.
Content
The book offers extensive access to the making of Gladiator II, detailing the recreation of ancient Rome through innovative practical sets, costumes, revolutionary special effects, and a blend of digital artistry. It highlights the challenges of scaling up the spectacle from the 2000 original while maintaining historical texture and cinematic ambition.
Key features include:
A foreword by Sir Ridley Scott, reflecting on the long development process (spanning over 25 years) and the importance of evolving the franchise.
Exclusive interviews with cast members such as Paul Mescal (Lucius), Denzel Washington, Pedro Pascal, Connie Nielsen, and others; plus crew insights from production designers, armorers, costume designers (including Janty Yates), cinematographers, and visual effects teams.
Rich visual documentation: Ridley Scott's hand-drawn "Ridleygrams," storyboards, concept art, character and costume sketches, unit photography from filming in Malta and Morocco, prop designs, set construction (e.g., Colosseum replicas), and ephemera.
Coverage of major sequences like gladiatorial combats, naval battles, and the integration of practical stunts with CGI.
Artistic inspirations drawn from 19th-century paintings by artists such as Jean-Léon Gérôme and Lawrence Alma-Tadema.
The volume positions itself as the definitive insider's guide to the film's creative and technical achievements.
Reception
The book has been well-received by critics and readers for its lavish production values, depth of insight, high-quality imagery, and value as a collectible companion to the film, with praise often focusing on its balance of visuals and informed commentary—even when reviewers had mixed feelings about the movie itself.
Karen Woodham of Blazing Minds awarded it 5 out of 5 stars, calling it an "incredible hardback" and a "fascinating insight into the making of Gladiator II," adding: "If, like me, you are into the world of film and particularly behind the scenes, then this book is a fascinating insight into the making of Gladiator II... If you’re a movie fan who enjoys behind-the-scenes insight, this book is a captivating read."
Back to the Movies gave it 4 out of 5, describing it as a "hefty coffee-table addition that should lay proud amongst any film fans collection," and noting: "John Walsh’s Gladiator II: The Art and Making of the Ridley Scott Film manages to strike the nice balance of visual spectacle and informed commentary... the book certainly props up the film and gives me that extra appreciation for it which speaks volumes on what John has created here. A real gift of a book to both casual admirers of the film and serious cinephiles."
Starburst Magazine praised it as a "lavish treasure trove of images and info," highlighting the design chapter: "The chapter on the film’s design is where the book shines. As well as some stunning photos and illustrations, there are quotes from the people who worked behind the scenes and details about the props and grand sets... Walsh covers every aspect of the film succinctly, often letting the images do the talking. The input from the creatives adds first-hand anecdotes that provide invaluable insight into the thought process behind the scenes. Fans of epic cinema will get a lot out of the book, and Gladiator fans will relish every page."
SciFiPulse emphasized its access and depth, stating that the book "packs a real punch, delivering a wealth of detail and insight that might just leave [readers] breathless," and describing it as providing "fascinating insights and... compelling stories from the major actors, writers, and producers involved in the project," with the foreword by Scott as a "standout feature."Yong How of
Halcyon Realms commended its comprehensive scope and visual highlights, writing: “This art and making-of-book is a very comprehensive coverage of all that, plus one more important item – Ridleygrams! Ridleygrams refer to the detailed color storyboards illustrated by the director himself as a pre-production tool for many of his films, and a very generous number is showcased in this book; certainly one of the bigger reasons why I decided to pick this up. There is still much to admire and enjoy about the excellent production value of this epic film. This art/making-of-book is the perfect volume to appreciate that.”
